hook: A runner jogs east, slows, turns around and sprints back. Her position, velocity and acceleration are a function and its first two derivatives. The exam asks about this kind of motion every year: which way is the particle going, is it speeding up, when does it turn around. Each answer comes from a sign.

prereq.q: $D'(4) = -3$ for a depth $D$ in meters and $t$ in hours means
options: at 4 hours the depth is decreasing at 3 meters per hour
the depth is 3 meters at 4 hours
the depth fell 3 meters in 4 hours
the depth is increasing at 3 meters per hour
prereq.why: A negative derivative is a decreasing quantity, at that rate.

figure.caption: For $x(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t$: velocity and acceleration, with shading where they share a sign (speeding up), and the path the particle traces on the line.

chain.effect: its rate of change is the velocity, $v(t) = x'(t)$
its rate of change is the acceleration, $a(t) = v'(t) = x''(t)$
gives the direction: right (or up) when $v > 0$, left when $v < 0$; a direction change needs $v$ to change sign
same sign: speeding up; opposite signs: slowing down

ideas: Velocity has a sign; speed is $|v(t)|$ and is never negative.
The particle is at rest when $v(t) = 0$, and changes direction only where $v$ changes sign.
Speeding up when $v$ and $a$ have the same sign. State both signs in a justification.
Units: position in meters gives velocity in meters per second and acceleration in meters per second per second.

misconception.wrong: Negative acceleration means the particle is slowing down.
misconception.right: It depends on the velocity too. With $v < 0$ and $a < 0$, the particle moves left faster and faster: it is speeding up. Slowing down needs $v$ and $a$ with opposite signs.

summary: For a particle on a line, $v(t) = x'(t)$ and $a(t) = v'(t) = x''(t)$. The sign of $v$ gives the direction, and the direction changes only where $v$ changes sign. Speed is $|v|$; it increases when $v$ and $a$ have the same sign and decreases when their signs differ.
